original_question: Let M be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold whose first Betti number is at least one. Let a ∈ H 2 (M ; R) be an (even) integral second cohomology class of dual Thurston norm one. Is there a finite cover p : M̃ → M and a taut foliation F of M̃ such that the Euler class e(F ) of F is equal to p∗ (a)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Question 2.1 ("Virtual Euler class one conjecture")
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s exact target. It matches the ambient class of manifolds (closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds with first Betti number at least one), the coefficient group H^2(M; R), the hypothesis that a is an (even) integral class of dual Thurston norm one, and the precise existence question about a finite cover p: M̃ -> M and a taut foliation F on M̃ with e(F) = p^*(a). It also correctly aims at the virtual realization problem for Euler classes of taut foliations, rather than the neighboring contact-structure questions.
missing_details: The paper explicitly names this statement Question 2.1, the "Virtual Euler class one conjecture"; adding that title pins down the target exactly.

In the surrounding setup, e(F) is defined for a (transversely oriented) taut foliation on a closed oriented 3-manifold as the Euler class of the oriented tangent plane field to F; your draft leaves this transversely oriented/oriented-plane-field setup implicit.

The paper explains the notation p^*(a) via Poincaré duality: it writes p^*: H1(M) -> H1(M̃) and identifies H1(M) ≅ H^2(M) and H1(M̃) ≅ H^2(M̃). Your draft uses p^*(a) without saying which identification/map is intended.
To be fully stand-alone, "an (even) integral class a in H^2(M; R)" should be unpacked as meaning that a lies in the image of H^2(M; Z) -> H^2(M; R) and is divisible by 2 there.
To be fully stand-alone, "dual Thurston norm one" should be identified as the dual norm on H^2(M; R) ≅ H1(M; R) induced by the Thurston norm.
refined_question: Question 2.1 (Virtual Euler class one conjecture). Let M be a closed oriented hyperbolic 3-manifold with b1(M) >= 1, and let a in H^2(M; R) be an even integral class of dual Thurston norm 1 (that is, a comes from H^2(M; Z) and is divisible by 2 there). Does there exist a finite-sheeted cover p: M̃ -> M and a transversely oriented taut foliation F on M̃ such that the Euler class e(F) of the oriented tangent plane field TF is equal to p^*(a), where p^*(a) is understood via the Poincaré duality identifications H1(M) ≅ H^2(M) and H1(M̃) ≅ H^2(M̃)?
justification: This is the exact statement your draft is trying to capture: §2.1 introduces Euler classes of taut foliations, recalls Thurston’s original Euler-class-one conjecture and its failure, and then states Question 2.1 in essentially the same form as your draft. The nearby paragraph supplies the hidden setup for e(F), and the sentence built into Question 2.1 supplies the Poincaré-duality interpretation of p^*(a). The immediately following Theorem 2.2 gives only partial positive evidence for rational dual-norm-one classes on certain manifolds, so the paper’s intended target here is still the narrower even-integral virtual realization question, not a broader rational or contact-structure variant.
